steps.question: Which genes differ significantly between treated and control muscle samples (padj<0.05, BH), fit once on all 10 samples (primary) and once excluding sample_03 (sensitivity), and how much does the gene list change between the two?

plan.title: Muscle DE: treated vs control (5v5, outlier check)
plan.analytical_narrative: Counts are raw gene-level integer counts from Salmon for 12,000 genes across 10 muscle samples (5 treated, 5 control, unpaired, single batch). Sample sample_03 separates from its group on PCA and the sample-distance heatmap, so the plan runs sample-structure QC first, investigates a technical cause for that departure, and then runs DESeq2 twice — once with all 10 samples (primary, per the flagged rule to keep and down-weight rather than silently drop an outlier at n=5/group) and once with sample_03 excluded (sensitivity) — reporting the overlap and the genes that change status between the two fits. A second DE method (edgeR quasi-likelihood) runs on the primary (all-sample) design as a robustness cross-check. Shrunken log2 fold changes (apeglm) are used for ranking and plotting; BH-adjusted p-values with independent filtering define the significant gene set (padj<0.05). The DESeq2 Wald statistic from the primary fit ranks genes for a preranked fgsea analysis against the MSigDB Hallmark human collection (staged at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human), with Reactome (/mnt/refs/managed/reactome-pathways) as the stated second collection. The final report consolidates both DE methods, both outlier-sensitivity fits, the enrichment results, and full reproducibility metadata (session info, package versions, gene-set collection versions).
